findings.message: Off by one. With `-n 120`, offset is 120 and the first line prints NR+offset = 121, not 120. The default case only works because an unset start gives offset 0. Default start to 1 and pass offset as START-1, or use `NR + start - 1`.

`lk_check_files number $@` lost its quotes (the original was `"$@"`; the other commands still use `"$@"`). File names containing spaces or glob characters are word-split and expanded, so valid files are rejected or the wrong files are checked. The awk call on line 35 still quotes `"$@"`, so the two calls now disagree. Restore `"$@"`.

No tests for `-n` were added to tests/t_number.sh. Missing cases: first line number, `-n 1`, `-n 0`, invalid values (`abc`, `-1`, empty), and numbering that continues across files. The first-line case would have caught the off-by-one error.
The digit check does not limit the range. Very large START values are passed to awk as doubles and printed with `%d`, so they can lose precision or overflow.

parsed.summary: Two defects confirmed. With `-n START`, the first line is numbered START+1 instead of START. Separately, `$@` lost its quotes in the file check. No tests cover `-n`. The range concern is minor.
